title: A person you met once and want to know more about
titleVi: Người bạn gặp một lần gần đây và muốn biết thêm
prompt: Describe a person you only met once recently and want to know more about
bullets: why you want to know more about him/her
and explain how you feel about him/her

notes.label: When / where
notes.text: a month ago, rainy Saturday, used bookshop on Đinh Lễ

part2.question: Describe a person you only met once recently and want to know more about

segments.v: I want to talk about an old man I met in a bookshop last month. I don't know his name. I went to a bookshop on Đinh Lễ street to buy some books. There was an old man and we wanted the same book. He gave the book to me and we talked. He told me that he was an architect before and he repaired old buildings in Hà Nội. He told me many interesting stories about old houses. I want to know more about him because he knows a lot about the history of Hà Nội. I want to ask him more questions about his work. I feel he is a very kind and interesting person. I am sad because I didn't ask his phone number. I went back to the bookshop but I didn't see him. I hope I will meet him again.

fluency.band6: Answers each bullet with one or two short sentences, in the same order; repeats “I want”, “He told me”; no scene-setting.
fluency.band9: Opens with the person and a hook (“which I'm still kicking myself about”), sets the scene, tells events in order, adds direct speech, then reflects on why and how. It flows like a real story and fills two minutes easily.

lexical.band6: old man, bookshop, repaired old buildings, interesting, kind, sad.
lexical.band9: elderly gentleman, got chatting to, kicking myself, struck up a conversation, it turned out, restoring, tracked down, warmth, humility, a walking archive, admiration, on the off chance.

grammar.band6: Mostly accurate but simple: past simple and “want to” repeated. Small issue: “he was an architect before” (better: “he used to be an architect”).
grammar.band9: Past perfect (had spent decades restoring), past continuous for background (We were both reaching for…), “so… that”, indirect questions (whether he kept sketches; how he feels about how fast…), and present perfect for the present link (I've been back twice).

analysis.keyDifference: Band 6 answers each bullet with a short sentence, repeats “I want” and “He told me”, and has no story shape. Band 9 sets the scene, tells what happened in order, uses direct speech, and reflects on feelings, keeping going naturally for two minutes.
